mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC's own week-over-week momentum predicts near-term continuation: the sharp rebound from -32.7 to -23.6 at t-0w indicates an active recovery trend in discretionary mobility that will carry forward into the immediate next week before any external shock reverses it.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose 9.1 points from t-1w (-32.7) to t-0w (-23.6)
failure_condition: If the mean RETAIL_REC over the next week falls below the t-0w value of -23.6, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility crosses above -5 percentage points from baseline, it signals a critical mass of outdoor/leisure activity that spills over into combined retail-and-recreation trips, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the following two weeks as households bundle outdoor and shopping errands.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -5 percentage points from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -11.1 at t-1w to -3.7 at t-0w, crossing the -5 threshold
failure_condition: If PARKS remains above -5 for two weeks but mean RETAIL_REC over that window declines relative to the prior four-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A divergence where WORKPLACES drops sharply week-on-week while TRANSIT stays essentially flat indicates a temporary holiday or localized closure rather than a broad lockdown; under this interaction, commuters substitute work trips with leisure trips, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks as the holiday effect normalizes into sustained discretionary activity.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES drops more than 5 points week-on-week while TRANSIT changes by less than 3 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -15.7 to -21.7 while TRANSIT only moved from -31.4 to -32.0 in the same week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT also drops sharply (more than 5 points) in the same or following week, indicating a broad lockdown rather than a holiday effect, or if RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next four weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has plateaued near 20 percent above baseline for four consecutive weeks, reflecting an entrenched behavioral caution baseline among residents; this steady-state caution regime caps the upside of any retail rebound, so despite recent gains RETAIL_REC's four-week trend will be flat to slightly negative rather than sustaining strong growth.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains within 19-21 percent for 4 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL held between 19.7 and 21.0 across all four observed weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL falls below 15 percent or RETAIL_REC continues to rise substantially over the next four weeks despite the residential plateau, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous sharp rise in PARKS and RETAIL_REC alongside a drop in WORKPLACES at t-0w is characteristic of a single holiday week rather than a structural shift; mobility patterns will partially revert within one week as work and commuting routines resume, pulling RETAIL_REC back down from its elevated t-0w level.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 5 points and WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose 7.4 points and WORKPLACES fell 6.0 points in the same t-0w week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues rising in the week immediately following the anomalous week without reverting toward the prior trend level, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility remaining persistently depressed near -32 percent despite rising RETAIL_REC signals ongoing public transit restrictions or rider reluctance; this transit bottleneck will constrain further RETAIL_REC growth over the next two weeks because reduced transit capacity limits consumer access to retail centers not reachable by private vehicle.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -30 percent for 2 or more consecutive weeks while RETAIL_REC is rising
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed between -34.6 and -31.4 across all four weeks while RETAIL_REC improved
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to rise strongly over the next two weeks despite TRANSIT remaining below -30 percent, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained positive GROCERY_PHARM mobility, consistently between 3 and 5 percent above baseline across all four observed weeks, indicates intact essential-trip capacity and household mobility access; this stable baseline supports continued recovery in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as discretionary trips resume on top of stable essential activity.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM ranged from 3.0 to 5.3 percent across all four weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM drops below 0 percent or RETAIL_REC declines over the next four weeks despite stable GROCERY_PHARM, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS and WORKPLACES both show simultaneous improvement (becoming less negative) over a trailing two-week window, it signals a coordinated loosening of restrictions across leisure and work domains; this combined easing accelerates consumer confidence and drives RETAIL_REC upward over the next two weeks beyond what either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and WORKPLACES both improve by more than 3 points over the trailing 2 weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -12.1 to -3.7 and WORKPLACES improved from -23.0 to -15.7 between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: If both PARKS and WORKPLACES improve over a two-week window but RETAIL_REC fails to rise or declines over the following two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.
